document_meta.title: Oregon State Wildlife Action Plan (SWAP) 2025 Draft

orientation.summary: This is Oregon's 2025/2026 draft State Wildlife Action Plan (SWAP), a comprehensive statewide conservation blueprint covering nine terrestrial ecoregions plus a nearshore marine ecoregion, Species of Greatest Conservation Need (SGCN), Key Habitats, Key Conservation Issues (KCIs), Conservation Opportunity Areas (COAs), monitoring guidance, and a Conservation Toolbox. The document takes a strongly engaged posture toward climate change as a 'threat multiplier' and dedicates an entire KCI chapter to it. It explicitly acknowledges climate-driven range shifts as an observed and projected phenomenon and proposes habitat connectivity, refugia identification, and spatial prioritization as adaptation strategies. The plan incorporates prior climate vulnerability analysis by reference but does not appear to perform new niche or climate modeling; climate projections (SSP585) from an external analysis (Raymond and Fusco, 2024) are incorporated into each ecoregion's climate section. The document integrates a nearshore appendix with detailed climate change fact sheets covering ocean acidification, hypoxia, warming temperatures, and species distribution shifts.
